last_result.mechanism: W2's near-constancy was never 'constancy with a scope'. It is this: if the FIRST list item is not decidable in the scenario, the model abstains (C) and the remaining four items effectively do not exist. Order B's first item (ShiZi has an instruction) is decidable in N3 because the scenario says 'no need to look again'; order A's first item (unread letter) is NOT decidable because N3 never mentions a letter.
last_result.deepest: The guard sentence does not improve judgement. It only shrinks the weight of the first item. When the first item is usually right, the guard is a net loss; when it is usually wrong, the guard rescues it. That is why it moved 14->13 and 12->13.

new_clauses.48: Before drawing a structure, look at HOW it grew. Check the first-seen distribution of the entries: clustered at a few timestamps = batch retrospection, evenly spread = filling in a tree. A batch-grown set can only be a heap, because each item answers one concrete incident and same-level items necessarily overlap. Drawing a tree over a heap is imposing a shape, not finding one. Measured: 27 of 37 clauses (73%) sit at two timestamps.
new_clauses.49: A 'do not only look at the first item' patch has an effect that depends entirely on the first item's hit rate: it does not improve judgement, it reallocates weight. If the first item is usually right, the patch is a net loss; if usually wrong, it rescues. And: if the first item is not decidable in the scenario, the model abstains and every later item becomes non-existent. (completes clause 21's trigger condition)
